stories.title: Legal challenge to Drumcree parade decision under way
stories.standfirst: Residents have applied to the High Court in Belfast to overturn the decision to allow a planned Orange Order parade on the mainly-nationalist Garvaghy Road in Portadown.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: The Parades Commission permitted the Orange Order to march along Garvaghy Road on Sunday with restrictions. The march must start by 08:00 BST with only 35 participants and no bands. The Garvaghy Road Residents' Coalition has challenged this decision at the High Court in Belfast.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: It would be the first march along this route in almost 30 years. A local Catholic priest warned the event could clash with Sunday Mass, noting high community tensions. Sinn Féin condemned the decision as reckless, while the Orange Order agreed to comply with the ruling and appealed for calm.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Judge Patricia Smyth adjourned the court hearing to seek a way forward in the limited time available. Meanwhile, police have arranged contingency operations for Sunday, with roughly 200 officers travelling from Scotland.
